topics.label: Lecture framing and introduction to cancer hallmarks
topics.groupedBecause: This opening establishes the lecture's learning outcomes and frames cancer hallmarks as a way to understand mutation-driven loss of growth control.

topics.label: Deregulation of growth and survival signalling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations in extracellular signalling pathways free cancer cells from normal controls on proliferation and survival.

topics.label: Differentiation blocks in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show how disrupted differentiation alters cancer-cell populations and tissue architecture.

topics.label: Resistance to apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how disruption of p53-dependent apoptotic regulation allows cancer cells to evade programmed death.

topics.label: Telomere maintenance and cancer-cell immortalization
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how telomere shortening limits normal cell replication and how telomerase reactivation enables cancer cells to bypass that limit.

topics.label: p53-mediated genome protection and growth-control recap
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics complete the account of mutation-driven loss of growth control by explaining p53's protective stress responses before recapping the hallmarks already discussed.

topics.label: Metabolic rewiring in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how altered metabolism supports cancer and participates in self-reinforcing changes to cellular regulation.

topics.label: Angiogenesis supporting tumour growth
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains why tumour growth requires an angiogenic switch that supplies oxygen and nutrients.

topics.label: Metastatic spread and establishment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer cells spread from a primary tumour and what determines their ability to establish detectable tumours at secondary sites.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and shared cancer hallmarks
topics.groupedBecause: This closing returns to the lecture's central message that diverse mutational routes converge on shared hallmarks and ends with reading guidance and practical-session signposting.
